title: GitOps signature guardrails & Helm operator upgrade plan
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working plan for adding signature verification guardrails to our GitOps-driven private deployments and a step-by-step upgrade path for the Helm-based operator used in on-prem clusters. Focus: automated CI signing/attestation, GitOps verification gates (ArgoCD + admission), Terraform module knobs for enforcing image policies, and safe rollout/rollback mechanics for operator upgrades.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Ensure only signed, attested images are accepted by customer clusters via GitOps pipeline and admission checks.
- Keep operator upgrades safe with canary traffic, automated health gates, and an emergency breakglass.
- Provide Terraform module flags that make enforcement repeatable for private deployments.
- Document manual and automated rollback paths with clear signals/metrics.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Customers use GitOps (ArgoCD) to apply Application manifests.
- Registry supports OCI manifests and immutable digests.
- We will prefer keyless cosign verification (OIDC) where possible, and KMS/HSM-backed keys for on-prem where required.
- No single global downtime window: upgrade should be incremental.

High-level flow (CI -> Registry -> GitOps -> Cluster):
1) CI pipeline (build) produces image + SBOM + attestation; sign with cosign (keyless or KMS).
   - Example: cosign sign --type=artifact --key ksm://projects/..../keys/helm-operator-signing-key <registry>/helm-operator@sha256:<digest>
   - Produce a simple attestation (predicate) including pipeline run id and Git commit. Upload to registry.
2) Terraform module (see notes) enforces an image acceptance_policy that can be: "off|signed-only|signed-and-sbom". This flips admission/webhook behavior in cluster.
3) Git branch -> pull request updates Helm values (image tag/digest); CI creates a signed tag and PR comment with signature verification metadata.
4) ArgoCD sync is gated by an admission controller that verifies signature + SBOM policy. If verification fails, auto-prune/sync is blocked and alert page created.

Terraform module notes (variables / patterns):
- module "private_cluster_policy" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@repo/terraform/modules/private-policy.git"
    image_accept_policy = var.image_accept_policy # off | signed-only | signed-and-sbom
    cosign_verifier_issuer = var.cosign_oidc_issuer # optional for keyless
    attestation_required = var.attestation_required # bool
    enforcement_mode = var.enforcement_mode # audit | enforce
  }
- State locking: ensure remote state backend with object lock (GCS/Azure) or S3 + DynamoDB for state locks.
- Workspaces: use separate workspaces for each customer environment (staging/prod) to avoid accidental global changes.
- Upgrade flag: module exposes helm_operator_image_digest and helm_operator_breakglass_annotation so infra can stage changes without changing values.yml directly.

Helm operator upgrade plan (stepwise):
1) Prepare release branch with operator chart bump and release notes. Add a config toggle: values.operator.rolloutStrategy = "canary".
2) CI builds operator image, signs it, publishes digest. PR includes digest and cosign verification output.
3) Apply to staging cluster (GitOps sync) with 10% canary: operator replicas: 1 canary, 9 stable (workload split handled by label-based placement).
4) Automated smoke tests (see test matrix) run for 30 minutes:
   - smoke checks: controller startup, leader election, reconcile loop success for 100 sample resources.
   - metrics: p95 reconcile latency, API errors, reconciler crashloop count.
5) If all gates pass, promote to 30% for 1h, then 60% for 1h, then full. Each promotion is an automated PR merge or ArgoCD promotion.
6) On failure, automatic rollback: revert to previous digest and trigger an immediate canary rollback + full rollback if severe.

Breakglass and emergency manual rollback:
- Breakglass annotation: values.operator.breakglass = true allows immediate forced revert by SRE via kubectl patch to the Application resource, bypassing normal promotion checks (requires 2 approvals in Slack #oncall plus JIRA PD-xxxx manual incident ticket).
- Documented kubectl steps for emergency: kubectl -n argocd patch application helm-operator -p '{"spec": {"source": {"targetRevision": "<previous-digest>"}}}' --type merge
- Post-rollback: create postmortem, run a forensic job that validates attestations and SBOM differences.

ArgoCD / Admission integration details:
- Use an admission webhook (in-cluster) that rejects deploys for images that don't meet module policy. Webhook queries cosign verifier service (local sidecar or central verifier) sending image digest and asking for verified=true.
- Where possible, prefer GitOps pre-verify hook: a plugin run during ArgoCD sync that checks for signature artifacts in the PR (this reduces noisy sync failures).
- Admission responses include a short failure reason pointing to the CI artifact link and the cosign log (to aid debugging).

Image signing and attestation pattern:
- Preferred flow (keyless): cosign sign --keyless --annotations pipeline_id=<id> <reg>/<image>@sha256:<digest>
- KMS-backed for private clusters that require keys: cosign sign --key ksm://projects/..../keys/helm-operator-signing-key <reg>/<image>@sha256:<digest>
- Verification: cosign verify --type=cosign <reg>/<image>@sha256:<digest>
- SBOM policy: for signed-and-sbom, verify SBOM presence and run a lightweight vulnerability policy (deny if critical CVEs with score>9 and not acknowledged).
- Record attestation: write verification result to the build artifact store and include link in PR.

CI pipeline snippets / suggestions:
- Build -> generate SBOM (syft) -> sign image (cosign) -> create attestation (in-toto predicate) -> run cosign verify locally -> push image -> create PR with digest+verify output.
- Example:
  ./scripts/build-image.sh && syft packages dir:./app -o json > sbom.json && COSIGN_PASSWORD=... cosign sign --key $KMS_REF $IMAGE && cosign verify $IMAGE && ./scripts/create-pr-with-digest.sh $IMAGE $SBOM_URL

Automated tests and health gates (signals):
- Functional: reconcile success for sample CRs, leader election, API responsiveness.
- Observability: p95 reconcile latency, error rates, container restart count.
- Business metric: if operator manages inference endpoints, measure 99th latency on a small synthetic workload.
- Define thresholds for automatic rollback. Example: p95 increase > 2x baseline or error rate > 1% for 10 minutes -> rollback.

Rollback tactics and artifacts to collect:
- On rollback, capture logs from new operator pods, stack traces, memory/CPU anomalies, and cosign verification logs.
- Keep a copy of SBOMs for both versions to aid triage.
- Store a reproducible CI job link (artifact id) that built the failing image.

Checklist (pre-upgrade runbook):
- [ ] All PRs signed and include cosign verification output.
- [ ] Terraform plan applied in staging workspace, enforcement_mode=audit.
- [ ] Confirm registry digest immutability for candidate images.
- [ ] Staging promotion completed and automated smoke tests green.
- [ ] SRE oncall designated for upgrade window.
- [ ] Breakglass playbook distributed to oncall and SEs.
- [ ] Notify customer(s) with optional maintenance window if operator changes affect endpoints.

Open questions / TODOs (short-term):
- Should we store cosign attestation metadata in a centralized ledger (gcs/dynamo) for audit? Pros: easy querying. Cons: storage/retention concerns.
- How to handle image pinning vs. float tags in customers that expect autopatching? propose terraform flag: allow_floating_tags = false by default.
- Add an operator-side health endpoint for faster ArgoCD probe feedback (reduce false negatives).

Appendix: useful commands
- Verify image signature: cosign verify --key ksm://... <reg>/<image>@sha256:<digest>
- Force ArgoCD to sync canary: argocd app sync helm-operator --server-side
- Patch Application to previous digest (rollback): kubectl -n argocd patch application helm-operator -p '{"spec": {"source": {"targetRevision": "<prev-digest>"}}}' --type merge
- Check SBOM with syft: syft packages dir:./app -o json

Notes from today's discussion (1/17):
- Lina: prefer OIDC-based keyless cosign for cloud-deployed CI; KMS only for on-prem where customers require HSM.
- Ravi: we need to make Terraform module defaults conservative (audit mode) and surface enforcement toggle clearly in onboarding docs.
- Marcus: investigate using attestation predicates for exact git SHA + CI run id so we can trace an image back to source quickly.

Next steps (owners assigned):
- [Sofia] Draft admission webhook spec and PR for a minimal verifier service (2 weeks).
- [Ravi] Add enforcement flags to terraform module and implement workspace tests (1 week).
- [Lina] Update CI templates to produce cosign artifacts and PR comments (1 week).
- [Marcus] Prototype canary promotion automation hooks in ArgoCD (2 weeks).

This is a working draft — expect iterations. Keep discussion in #eng-private-deploy and link PRs to JIRA:PD-912 for traceability.
